title: The Two Weeks Korean Mothers Book After Giving Birth

slides.headline: Korean mothers **check into a hotel** after birth.
slides.note: Not a hospital, not home. A paid building with one job: getting the mother back on her feet.

slides.headline: It has a name: **sanhujoriwon (산후조리원)**
slides.body: A postpartum care centre. Mothers move in straight from the delivery hospital and stay about two weeks.

slides.headline: Korea has a rulebook for **the first weeks**
slides.body: Sanhujori (산후조리) says a new mother stays warm, stays still and eats seaweed soup while her body closes back up.

slides.headline: **Samchilil (삼칠일)**: the first 21 days
slides.body: The old custom shut the house for three weeks. No visitors, no cold air, no cold water. The centre is its modern form.

slides.headline: the standard **sanhujoriwon stay**
slides.body: Meals arrive on a schedule, the room stays warm, and the nights belong to somebody else.

slides.headline: The nursery is **the whole point**
slides.body: Newborns stay in a staffed room around the clock. Mothers come in for feeds, then go back to sleep.

slides.headline: Elsewhere you go **straight home**
slides.body: Most countries send a mother back to her own bed and her own 3am. Korea built a building for that fortnight instead.

slides.headline: **Joriwon dongi (조리원 동기)**: friends by accident
slides.body: Mothers whose stays overlap become a group chat. Some of them are still in it when the kids start school.

slides.headline: Recovery here is **a place you book**
slides.body: Not a favour from family, not time off. A reservation, made months before the due date.

slides.headline: Korea, explained **by a Korean.**
slides.body: Follow for the context behind the things Korea does.

caption:
In Korea a mother does not go home after giving birth — she checks into a sanhujoriwon, a postpartum care centre, and stays about two weeks.

It comes from sanhujori, the old rule that the weeks after birth are for staying warm and still, not for hosting visitors. The modern version books it as a room: meals on a schedule, a staffed nursery overnight, and the first real sleep since the delivery room.

The side effect nobody plans for is the group chat. Mothers who overlap at the same centre call each other joriwon dongi, and some of those chats outlive the babies' first school year.

Where does a new mother go in your country?
reply:
One thing that did not fit on the cards: the centres run classes while you are in there — bathing, feeding, swaddling — so the two weeks double as training. You leave with a routine, not just rest.

fact_check: 이용률·평균 비용은 조사연도와 지역(특히 서울)에 따라 편차가 크다. 카드와 캡션에 수치를 넣지 않았다. 넣게 되면 보건복지부 산후조리 실태조사 최신판을 근거로 달 것.
'약 2주'는 일반적인 표준 상품 기준이다. 1주·3주 상품도 있으므로 '평균'이 아니라 '표준'으로 표현했다.
삼칠일(21일)은 전통 관습이며 현행 조리원 기간과 직접 연결되는 제도가 아니다. 카드에서도 '옛 관습의 현대판'으로만 서술했다.
신생아실 운영 방식(24시간 상주 인력, 모자동실 여부)은 시설마다 다르다. 특정 시설 기준으로 단정하지 않았다.
